problem: Existing MLLM-based zero-shot VLN agents use a tightly coupled design that infers global spatial structure implicitly from egocentric RGB streams or oversimplified textual maps. This yields hallucinated layouts, spatial errors that propagate into semantic reasoning, and inflexible reasoning strategies.
motivation: Zero-shot MLLM agents avoid costly fine-tuning and keep the models' generalization, but they lack a consistent, geometrically grounded world model. The authors observe that decoupling spatial state estimation from semantic planning, and giving the MLLM an explicit metric map to interact with, lets it produce physically valid waypoints and transfer across embodiments.
key_idea: Decouple spatial estimation (a TSDF metric map plus topological graph rendered as a BEV with coordinate grid) from semantic planning, and let a frozen MLLM do counterfactual, checklist-guided reasoning to output a pixel waypoint that is ray-cast into a 3D goal.
insight: Adding the explicit world representation (EWR) to other agents (NavGPT, OpenNav, SmartWay) consistently improves SR; for example SmartWay goes from 34.4 to 41.1 on the R2R-CE subset, so the gain comes from the representation. Removing the procedural blueprint lowers OSR from 56.7 to 48.3, showing the checklist keeps long-horizon semantic consistency. Performance scales with backbone strength (Qwen3-VL-235B 37.2 < Gemini-2.5 Pro 42.3 < GPT-5.1 47.2 SR), indicating a plug-and-play interface.
method: Metric Mapping Module: fuses RGB-D from a rotating camera into a TSDF volume via weighted running-average integration, giving a consistent collision-free metric map.
Topological graph G_topo: nodes hold metric position and visit count, merged within 0.8 m; used for loop detection and backtracking alerts, and to report vertical state (up/downstairs at |Δh|>0.3 m).

Interactive Reasoning Interface: selects four orthogonal RGB-D views (0/90/180/270°) near the current position, renders the TSDF as a top-down BEV via orthographic projection, and overlays a normalized [0,1000]^2 coordinate grid on the BEV and egocentric views as the visual prompt.

Procedural Reasoning Blueprints: decomposes the instruction into a dynamic TODO checklist that the MLLM updates every step; the prompt also includes topological state, safety alerts, a 5-step sliding-window history and the global instruction.
Counterfactual Reasoning Brain: a frozen MLLM evaluates candidate actions against the goal list via 'what if' rollouts on the map and outputs JSON with reasoning, a view ID and normalized (u,v).

Spatial Action Decoding & Execution: ray-casts (u,v) onto the TSDF mesh to obtain a 3D waypoint, which a deterministic local planner (Nav2 in the real world) executes; loop detection triggers re-planning.

setting.backbone: GPT-5.1 (frozen) for main results; Gemini-2.5 Pro and Qwen3-VL-235B in ablation
setting.observation: RGB-D from four orthogonal views (rotating camera panoramic scan) plus estimated pose; TSDF-built BEV map
setting.action_space: predicted continuous local waypoint (pixel to ray-cast 3D target), executed by a deterministic local planner
setting.simulator: Habitat (R2R-CE, RxR-CE); real TurtleBot 4 and custom quadrotor
setting.privileged: none (pose estimation assumed; drone uses external motion capture for state estimation)

numbers_note: The RxR-CE SR in the abstract and text (42.2%) conflicts with Table 1 (46.2). The backbone for the main tables is not stated explicitly; GPT-5.1 is inferred. Ablations use a self-curated 180-episode hard subset of R2R-CE. The R2R/REVERIE and discrete-environment EWR tables also exist but are only partly listed.
results: GTA reaches 48.8 SR / 41.8 SPL on the full R2R-CE val-unseen and 46.2 SR (Table 1; 42.2 in the text) on a 260-episode RxR-CE subset, beating the best prior zero-shot method BZS-VLN (41.0 SR on R2R-CE; 35.7 SR on RxR-CE). In the real world it achieves 40% SR (wheeled) and 42% (drone), versus SmartWay 32%, VLN-BERT 16% and RDP 20%. It still trails supervised Efficient-VLN (64.2 SR).
limitations: Depends on a proprietary MLLM (GPT-5.1) and multiple MLLM calls per step, giving high latency and cost. Results drop sharply with weaker backbones.
Assumes reliable pose estimation and a rotating RGB-D camera; the drone relies on external motion capture. Dynamic scenes and open-vocabulary 3D perception are left for future work.
RxR-CE is evaluated on only a 260-episode subset and ablations on a self-curated 180-episode subset, limiting comparability; the paper also has an SR inconsistency between text and table.
